I’ve ordered from this place twice on Zomato since we are from Hyderabad and wanted to try their biryani. Both times, I ordered the Hyderabadi Chicken Dum Biryani and the Lucknow Biryani.

Unfortunately, they didn’t follow the cooking instructions on either occasion, even though I mentioned that the order was specially prepared for us. I had clearly asked for it to be spicy 🌶️, but it wasn’t. I also requested cutlery both times—they missed it the first time, and again the second time. I also ordered Phirni. The first time, it tasted really good, so I ordered two portions the second time—but the taste was so bad that I had to throw them away.

Even the Salan (gravy) was inconsistent. The first time, it was tasty though a bit watery. This time I ordered two portions (one large and one small), and both were a disaster — very thin and lacking flavor.

Overall, Banana Leaf delivers excellent food with authentic flavors, making it a good choice for South Indian cuisine lovers. Ishara – A must-visit for food + vibe + meaning

Ambience: Absolutely beautiful. The restaurant has different seating areas so it never feels cramped, and when I visited there was live music that added to the whole experience. Great spot for a relaxed dinner with friends or a date.

Staff & Philosophy:What stood out most was the staff. Everyone was incredibly friendly and accommodating. You don’t need to know sign language at all; the floor managers are there to help and make communication smooth. It made the service feel warm and personal.

1. Virgin Mojito – Refreshing and spot on.
2. Mushroom Galawat Kebab– Must try!A vegetarian galouti kebab that’s super soft, melts in your mouth, and is packed with flavor.

4. Dilli Papdi Chaat– Light, fresh, and a good palate cleanser.

6. Moplah Chemeen Biryani (Prawn Biryani)– _Must try main course._ Cooked with coconut milk and mild spices, the prawns were juicy and flavorful. It’s not your typical biryani — the rice is a bit mushy, but it works perfectly with the dish.
7. Rasmalai Tres Leches– A fusion that leans more traditional rasmalai. Rich, and easily shareable for 2 people.

featured_reviews.name: Prachiti Gadekar

featured_reviews.name: Tasty fiesta

featured_reviews.name: rajesh jaiswar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Ishaara at Palladium recently and it turned out to be a memorable dining experience—not just for the food, but for the overall concept and service.

The ambience is elegant yet calming, with a minimalistic design that allows you to relax and enjoy your meal without too much noise or distraction. It feels premium but still comfortable enough for a casual outing.

What really stands out is their unique service model, where the staff communicates through sign language. Despite that, the service is extremely smooth, attentive, and warm. You genuinely feel the effort and hospitality, which adds a special emotional value to the experience.

Coming to the food, we tried a variety of dishes:

* Nihari Soup – Deep, rich, and full of flavour. A great start to the meal, especially if you enjoy slow-cooked, meaty broths.
* Chicken Roll – Nicely done, with good balance of spices and texture. Simple but satisfying.
* Palak Paneer Kofta – Soft koftas with a creamy spinach gravy, slightly on the indulgent side but very comforting.
* Mutton Champaran – One of the highlights. Well-cooked, aromatic, and packed with bold spices. You can taste the slow cooking in every bite.
* Dindigul Biryani – Fragrant with a mild tangy note, distinct from regular biryanis. Well-layered and flavourful without being too heavy.

The menu beautifully brings together regional Indian flavours, and each dish feels thoughtfully prepared rather than overly commercial.

If I had to point out anything, it would be that portion sizes could feel slightly moderate for the price point—but the quality and experience make up for it.

Overall, Ishaara is not just about dining—it’s about experiencing food with purpose. Great food, meaningful service, and a peaceful ambience make it worth visiting.

featured_reviews.name: Bhavin Parekh

Yazu is a Pan‑Asian “supper club” concept that brings together flavors from Japan, China, Thailand, Korea and Southeast Asia under one roof. The Lower Parel outlet is positioned as a flagship. The place is spacious combining indoor and outdoor elements. The branding emphasizes “visual experiences” — sculptural ceiling installations, patterned concrete flooring, carved wooden walls, lighting as focal décor elements. Ambience is amazing: stylish, atmospheric, good for evenings, date nights, or a premium outing. The décor and lighting get special and the ceiling installation, carved walls, and an aesthetic that’s “Instagram‑worthy.” After sundown, it transforms into a high‑energy bar/music venue  like “Studio Nights”.
Wide and ambitious menu: sushi, sashimi, maki, dim sum, baos (Taiwanese street bun), Teppanyaki, Robata grill items, curries, fusion dishes (e.g. “Asian Pizza‑San”) etc. They offer special dietary menus: Jain and Keto options. Go for signature dishes (e.g. sushi rolls, baos, dim sum) early; save room for dessert.
Top Picks:
• Black crispy Asparagus Roll (sushi) • Steamed Veg. Cheung Fung • Veg. Dimsum Experience Basket (7 piece) • Spicy Lotus root • Mah Poh Tofu etc.
• For soups: the Tom Kha, Tom Yum are superb.
• Desserts are also a highlight: “Pull Me Up Tiramisu”, “Berry Blossom Cheesecake”, “Salted Caramel Tart”, Coconut Panna Cotta etc. Presentation is premium, textures and flavors seem well balanced in many reviews.
• Drinks are highly inventive, globally inspired, and expertly crafted. Every sip is bold and gives unforgettable experience. Loved its Samurai (cocktail), Shojo and Yashi (mocktails) which were flavorful and refreshing.
Attentive and polite staff who guide through the menu, make recommendations, and ensure a comfortable dining experience. Yazu Lower Parel is a strong pick if you're looking for a premium Pan‑Asian dining + bar experience in Mumbai. The ambience, décor, and overall concept are standout features. The place has a premium, elegant vibe and delivers a memorable night out.

Our lunch at Punjab Grill, Phoenix Palladium Mall, turned out to be one of the most satisfying and comforting North Indian meals we’ve had in Mumbai. Being from North India, we always look for places that can recreate authentic flavours, and Punjab Grill once again lived up to expectations with its rich taste, warm ambience, and excellent service.

We ordered our all-time favourites — Dal Makhani and Paneer Lababdar, accompanied by Lachha Paranthas, Tandoori Rotis, and fresh salads. The Dal Makhani was slow-cooked to perfection, creamy, smoky, and just the right amount of buttery, reminding us of dhabas back home. The Paneer Lababdar was equally delicious: soft paneer cubes in a luscious, mildly spicy gravy that paired beautifully with the hot, crisp Lachha Paranthas. The Tandoori Rotis were perfectly roasted, light, and complemented the curries well. Every dish carried an unmistakable authentic North Indian aroma and taste.

The ambience of the restaurant added to the experience — elegant but cosy, with comfortable seating and warm lighting that made the meal feel unhurried and enjoyable. The environment was calm despite the mall rush, making it a great spot to relax after a movie.

What truly stood out was the courteous and attentive staff. They served promptly, checked in without being intrusive, and ensured every dish was fresh and hot. At the end of the meal, the liquid mouth freshener served in tiny tequila-style glasses was a delightful touch — refreshing, unique, and a fun way to conclude the lunch.

Overall, Punjab Grill offered a wonderful blend of flavour, comfort, and hospitality. For anyone craving authentic North Indian food in Mumbai, this place is always a dependable choice. A memorable lunch indeed!
